note: The closed vocabulary of the commitment form (ADR 0005). Every word the model may use when it commits is an entry here, with its meaning. A word that is not here cannot be committed. Hand-edited; shared/form_schema_v1.json and docs/CATALOGUE.md are generated from it by 'python3 -m lang.form write'.

general.meaning: Plain geometry and annotation that belongs to no trade: rectangles, circles, lines, text.

mechanical.meaning: Flat parts and their features: plates, holes, slots, fillets, chamfers.

architecture.meaning: Building plans: rooms, walls and what is hosted in them.

civil.meaning: Site and infrastructure plans: plots, roads, parking, pipes, manholes.

schematic.meaning: Circuit and connection diagrams: symbols joined by wires.

add.meaning: Put a new object in the drawing. The name must be new.

change.meaning: Change dimensions, properties, relations or text of an object that already exists.

remove.meaning: Take an existing object out of the drawing. Nothing but its name is given.

length.meaning: A distance on the sheet in real-world units; needs a length unit.

angle.meaning: A rotation; needs an angle unit.

count.meaning: A whole number of things; takes no unit.

width.meaning: The extent across the object, perpendicular to its length; for hosted objects, along the host.

height.meaning: The vertical extent on the sheet; for doors and windows, the real-world height of the opening.

length.meaning: The long extent of the object, along its main axis.

depth.meaning: How far the object reaches into its host or away from the viewer; for blind holes, the drilled depth.

thickness.meaning: The thickness of a wall or a plate.

diameter.meaning: The diameter of a round object; for a regular polygon, the circumscribed circle.

radius.meaning: The radius of a round object or of a fillet.

sill_height.meaning: The height of a window's sill above the floor.

distance.meaning: A gap between two things, measured edge to edge unless the relation says otherwise.

angle.meaning: A rotation, counter-clockwise from the horizontal.

sides.meaning: How many sides a regular polygon has.

side.meaning: Which side of the target the object goes on.

left.meaning: Towards the left of the sheet from the target.

right.meaning: Towards the right of the sheet from the target.

above.meaning: Towards the top of the sheet from the target.

below.meaning: Towards the bottom of the sheet from the target.

axis.meaning: The direction along which two things line up.

horizontal.meaning: Same height on the sheet: centres on one horizontal line.

vertical.meaning: Same position across the sheet: centres on one vertical line.

on.meaning: Hosted by the target: a window on a wall, a hole on a plate, a junction on a wire.
on.frame: The host. Says what the object belongs to and fixes no position by itself: another relation says where on the host.

inside.frame: The target's outline. A check, not a place: the object must lie within it, and another relation says where.

centred_on.meaning: The object's centre coincides with the target's centre; on a wall, the wall's midpoint along its length.
centred_on.frame: The target's centre (a wall's midpoint). The object's centre goes there: fixes left-right and up-down.

along.meaning: Runs along the whole length of the target, on the given side if one is named.
along.frame: The target's edge on the named side, or its long axis when no side is named. The object lies against that edge, outside the target (or on the axis), and starts where the target starts: fixes the place across the edge, and along it by default.

offset_from.meaning: At the given distance from the target, on the given side.
offset_from.frame: The target's edge on the named side. The object's facing edge is the given distance beyond it: fixes the place across that edge; along it, by default, the two are flush at the left (above, below) or at the bottom (left, right).

next_to.meaning: Touching the target, on the given side.
next_to.frame: The target's edge on the named side. The object's facing edge touches it: fixes the place across that edge; along it, by default, the two are flush at the left (above, below) or at the bottom (left, right).

between.meaning: Spans from the first target to the second: a wire between two terminals, a wall between two rooms.
between.frame: The two targets' reference points (centres of round things and symbols); when both are rectangles that touch along an edge, that shared edge (D-005). The object spans from the first to the second, its axis on that line: fixes both. Only straight things span between.

aligned_with.meaning: Lined up with the target along the given axis.
aligned_with.frame: The target's centre. On axis horizontal the centres are at the same height (fixes up-down); on axis vertical they are on one vertical line (fixes left-right).

distributed_over.meaning: The given number of copies, equally spaced over the target.
distributed_over.frame: The target's long axis. The copies are equally spaced along it, N copies with N + 1 equal spaces between the target's ends and their centres (D-004; fixes that direction), and, by default, centred across it. Needs the target's direction to be known.

at.meaning: The object's reference point coincides with the target's: 'at origin' anchors the first object of a drawing.
at.frame: The target's reference point. The object's reference point goes there: fixes both.

top.meaning: The target's top edge: the horizontal line along its top, from its left side to its right side. 'offset from plate1 top by 15 mm on side below' puts the object's top 15 mm under it.

bottom.meaning: The target's bottom edge: the horizontal line along its bottom.

left.meaning: The target's left edge: the vertical line along its left side.

right.meaning: The target's right edge: the vertical line along its right side.

top_left.meaning: The target's top-left corner: one point.

top_right.meaning: The target's top-right corner: one point.

bottom_left.meaning: The target's bottom-left corner: one point.

bottom_right.meaning: The target's bottom-right corner: one point.

origin.meaning: The origin of the drawing: the point (0, 0) of the sheet. Always exists; cannot be added, changed or removed. The first object of a drawing is placed at origin.

sheet.meaning: The one frame every position is finally measured in: x to the right, y up, from origin. left, right, above and below are directions on the sheet, never relative to an object's own rotation.

box.meaning: Rectangular things (rectangle, plate, room, plot, square column, parking bay): the lower-left corner.

round.meaning: Round things (circle, hole, threaded hole, manhole, round column, regular polygon) and schematic symbols: the centre.

text.meaning: Text: the start of its baseline.

line.meaning: Straight things (line, wall, road, pipe, wire, slot): the start of their axis.

thread.meaning: ISO metric coarse thread of a threaded hole.

hole_type.meaning: Whether a hole goes all the way through its host.

through.meaning: All the way through the host.

corner.meaning: Which corner of the host a corner feature goes on.

top_left.meaning: The top-left corner on the sheet.

top_right.meaning: The top-right corner on the sheet.

bottom_left.meaning: The bottom-left corner on the sheet.

bottom_right.meaning: The bottom-right corner on the sheet.

hinge_side.meaning: Which jamb of a door carries the hinges, seen from the side it opens towards.

swing.meaning: Which way a door opens relative to the room it belongs to.

pipe_use.meaning: What a pipe carries; decides its layer and line style.

orientation.meaning: How a schematic symbol lies on the sheet.

line.meaning: A straight line; where it starts and ends comes from its relations.

regular_polygon.meaning: A regular polygon inscribed in a circle of the given diameter.

text.meaning: A line of text; its height comes from the drawing standard unless given.

plate.meaning: The outline of a flat rectangular part.

hole.meaning: A plain round hole in a plate.

threaded_hole.meaning: A tapped hole; the drill and thread diameters come from the thread size.

slot.meaning: A straight slot with round ends; length is overall, width is the end diameter.

fillet.meaning: A rounded corner of a plate.

chamfer.meaning: A 45-degree bevel on a corner of a plate; length is the leg.

room.meaning: A rectangular room, given by its internal size; its walls follow from the standard.

wall.meaning: A straight wall; its thickness comes from the standard unless given.

door.meaning: A hinged door in a wall, with its swing drawn.

opening.meaning: A plain opening in a wall, with no door or window.

column.meaning: A column: square if given a width, round if given a diameter.

road.meaning: A straight road carriageway, drawn as its two edges and centreline.

parking_bay.meaning: One parking bay; its size comes from the standard unless given.

pipe.meaning: A buried pipe, drawn as a single line in the style of what it carries.

resistor.meaning: A resistor symbol; its text is the designator, such as R1.

capacitor.meaning: A capacitor symbol; its text is the designator.

switch.meaning: A single-pole switch symbol; its text is the designator.

lamp.meaning: A lamp symbol; its text is the designator.

terminal.meaning: A connection terminal; its text is its label.

wire.meaning: A wire joining two symbols or terminals; routed by the solver.

junction.meaning: A connection dot on a wire.
